chunks: Is one who is devout in the watches of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, (like one who does not)? Say: 'Can those who know and those who do not know be equal?' Only they remember who are people of intellect.

key_terms.آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ: The watches of the night, periods of the night
key_terms.أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ: People of intellect, those endowed with reason
key_terms.قَانِتٌ: Devout, obedient, one who performs acts of worship with humility

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between those who know and those who do not know according to this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this verse highlights the spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt and the righteous, who maintain constant vigilance (Muraqabah) through night prayers, embodying the balance between fear of divine retribution and hope for mercy. The concluding rhetorical question underscores that true knowledge (Ilm) is not merely intellectual but is intrinsically linked to piety and introspection, a key theme in Nahj al-Balagha. It serves as a reminder that divine wisdom is accessible only to those who possess deep insight (Ulul Albab) and apply it to their spiritual conduct.
